question: In uncomplicated primary monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis, non-pharmacological interventions — including an enuresis alarm and motivational therapy — are recommended as the first-line treatment before resorting to pharmacotherapy such as desmopressin.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Non-pharmacological management — enuresis alarm, motivational charts, fluid and voiding advice, bladder training — is first-line. Desmopressin is effective but best reserved for cases where alarm therapy fails, is impractical (e.g. family or sleeping-environment constraints), or for short-term control (e.g. overnight stays).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Clinical guidelines (NICE, ICCS) recommend behavioural and alarm-based therapies as the foundation of treatment for primary monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis. The enuresis alarm has the highest long-term cure rate. Desmopressin (a synthetic ADH analogue that reduces nocturnal urine production) is effective but has a higher relapse rate on discontinuation, and is used when the alarm is impractical or as adjunct therapy.
